text:
sam: quick spotcheck from today's GPTQ bakeoff across model families. ran GPTQ 4-bit (our tuned recipe) + baseline AWQ-int8 on Llama-2-13b, Mistral-7B-v0.1, Qwen-7B-mini across a short eval suite (HellaSwag, MMLU-10-subset, commonsense, code-samples). uploading artifacts: s3://redwood-inference/bakeoffs/1768504321/ :point_down:

liam: link? can you drop the summary numbers inline? :eyes:

sam: sure — high level deltas vs fp16 baseline (accuracy points):
```
Model      | GPTQ-4bit Δ | AWQ-int8 Δ | Notes
Llama-13b  | -2.3 pts     | -0.9 pts   | big HellaSwag drop, odd tokenization on longer context
Mistral-7B | -0.8 pts     | -0.6 pts   | stable on MMLU, code samples worse
Qwen-7B    | -0.4 pts     | -0.2 pts   | smallest regressions, some RMSE shift in generation length
```

sara: whoa Llama -2.3 on MMLU? that's higher than expected. which prompts/seq len?

sam: default eval used seq_len=1024 for MMLU. we also ran a 2048 pass and saw HellaSwag go down another ~1.2 for Llama. looks like prefix Kv-cache packing issues with our GPTQ kernels at long contexts.

jia: we saw a pattern where GPTQ quant preserves top-1 but hurts calibration on multiple-choice. HellaSwag is sensitive to that. AWQ-int8 keeps logits scale better for those tasks.

nick: any perf numbers? throughput/latency?

sam: latency (p95) tokens/sec approximations on a T4-like test instance (batch=1 streaming):
```
Model      | FP16 tok/s | GPTQ-4bit tok/s | AWQ-Int8 tok/s
Llama-13b  | 120        | 190             | 175
Mistral-7B | 220        | 340             | 320
Qwen-7B    | 210        | 305             | 290
```
so GPTQ gives best perf win but incurs accuracy delta for Llama. AWQ gives smaller speedup but better accuracy retention in some families.

liam: do we have per-task breakdowns? especially codegen (small snippets) — Mistral flagged as worse?

sam: yes — quick extract for CodeQA-ish subset:
- Mistral GPTQ: -3.5 pts on pass@1 for small code tasks (likely due to numeric jitter on logits leading to beam differences).
- Llama GPTQ: -1.5 pts pass@1.
- Qwen GPTQ: -0.6 pts.
AWQ-int8 tends to keep pass@1 within 0.5 pts of fp16 for all three.

sara: are these deterministic? couldn't we change our GPTQ kernel ordering to stabilize?

jia: some of it looks non-deterministic across runs; we saw run-to-run variance ~0.2-0.6 pts for GPTQ on Mistral in 3 repeats. AWQ much lower variance.

nick: operationally, what's the deployment recommendation for Dedicated?

sam: proposal: for Dedicated pools serving generative code or long-context MMLU-like workloads, prefer AWQ-int8 until we fix GPTQ KV-cache ordering and calibration. For high-throughput cheap text generation (chat summary short replies) GPTQ-4bit is acceptable for Mistral/Qwen but hold off on Llama-13b.

liam: can we add a lightweight prompt/regression trigger? e.g., run small probe set on every model/build and fail rollout if any task drops >1.0 pt?

sam: yep — I'll wire a canary with 12 probes (HellaSwag, MMLU-10, CodeQA-20, tox-check quick). current recommended threshold: no model family should drop >1.0 pts MMLU or >2.0 pts on any single probe.

eval-bot: bakeoff artifacts uploaded. summary CSV: s3://redwood-inference/bakeoffs/1768504321/summary.csv. bench logs: s3://redwood-inference/bakeoffs/1768504321/logs/

jia: FYI we also tried a hybrid route: per-layer mixed quant (GPTQ on attention only + AWQ for feedforward). that kept perf ~GPTQ-4bit but accuracy closer to AWQ. early results promising, need more runs.

nick: capture operational cost delta? customers will ask about dollars/token.

sam: rough USD per 1M tokens estimate (on spot-equivalent infra): FP16 = $8.2, AWQ-int8 = $4.7, GPTQ-4bit = $3.1. numbers rough and depend on batching.

liam: next steps?

sam: action items:
- sam: run 5-repeat stability runs for Mistral GPTQ + hybrid config (due EOD tomorrow)
- jia: validate prompt-set canary and add to pipeline (due Tue)
- nick: draft recommended deploy matrix for Dedicated + Private (AWQ for long-context/code, GPTQ for short chat where acceptable) (due Fri)
- sara: triage the Llama tokenization edgecase and try alternative tokenizers in eval harness (due Wed)

liam: thanks. adding :thumbsup: I'll schedule a quick follow-up sync Wed 10am to review hybrid results.

sam: sounds good. ping me if anyone needs the raw binaries or to reproduce locally. I put the quant recipes in the artifacts dir.

sara: nice work — this helps us make clearer defaults for onboarding new models. :party:
